title: 4-bit right-shift, left-shift register

sources.document: TI The TTL Data Book for Design Engineers, 2nd ed. 1976, section 7 (MSI/LSI data sheets)
sources.familyUsed: SN7495A (the 1976 book lists only the A version of the plain 74 part)

pins.name: MODE
pins.text: mode control: high = parallel load / shift left on CK2, low = shift right on CK1

functions.text: Register stage A (QA is the stage the serial input enters).
Register stage B (QA is the stage the serial input enters).
Register stage C (QA is the stage the serial input enters).
Register stage D (QA is the stage the serial input enters).

state.changesOn: falling edge of CK1 (MODE low) or of CK2 (MODE high)
rules: MODE high, falling edge of CK2: QA QB QC QD = A B C D (parallel load; CK1 is ignored, serial entry is inhibited)
Shift left = parallel load with QB wired to A, QC to B, QD to C, and serial data on D
MODE low, falling edge of CK1: QA = SER, QB = old QA, QC = old QB, QD = old QC (shift right; CK2 is ignored)

Changes on MODE should be made while both clocks are low; the function table also shows hold for MODE rising with CK2 L CK1 L, MODE falling with CK2 L CK1 L, MODE falling with CK2 L CK1 H, MODE rising with CK2 H CK1 L, and MODE rising with CK2 H CK1 H

timing.conditions: VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 15 pF, RL 400 ohm
VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 15 pF, RL 400 ohm

notes: MODE is drawn as an input: it chooses which clock and which data path is used; it does not switch the outputs off. The datasheet gives no minimum propagation delays; the path-delay function uses 0 ns for the minimum.
